gen-dafont-origami-gf-atkinson-hyperlegi: Origami looks like a sign-painter's brush held at constant width. Atkinson Hyperlegible, a plain sans with clipped capitals, is the opposite: no brush swell anywhere in it, just wide-set terminals on the s.

Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono spaces its letters far apart, like stencil bridges stretched open, with counters that breathe. And Origami, heavy and brushy up top, packs its lowercase into a dense mass, so size the mono text up a touch.

Origami pairs a sign-painter's single-stroke brush look with a lowercase mass like poured lead type. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next brings big lowercase eyes and rounds left unlatched, which gives the heading's dense weight room to breathe.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-biryani: A brush-painted, single-stroke look at constant width gives Origami its dense, lead-type lowercase heft. Biryani sits beneath it, sans-serif and unclogged, with large open eyes on every e.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-blinker: Contemporary and a bit unusual, Origami lays down single brush strokes at constant width in a heavy lowercase mass. Blinker follows in a plain sans with open apertures and tall lowercase, so a long passage reads smoothly and easily.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-carrois-gothic: Unique in its single-stroke brush look, Origami holds one pen pressure and angle from start to finish in every letter. Carrois Gothic answers plainly beneath.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Contemporary in feel, Origami draws every letter with one constant line width, like a sign-painter's brush that never presses harder. Carrois Gothic SC, a plain sans, keeps a clear opening at each curve and little gap between capital and lowercase height, so longer text moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-chivo: Dense, brushed, and blunt: Origami cuts every stroke to one width. Chivo, a plain sans with lowercase packed up toward the caps and daylight in every curve, gives that weight somewhere lighter to land.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-chocolate-classica: Origami opens with a sign-painter's single-stroke brush look, its lowercase massed like poured lead type. Chocolate Classical Sans, a sans-serif with a sizable lowercase and a broad-nibbed stroke that never curls shut, keeps a longer passage easy to move through.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-comme: Unique and brush-drawn, Origami uses a marker-nib line that ignores direction, so it earns its keep big and short. And Comme, a smooth sans with lowercase bodies filling most of the letter height, takes over for the running text.
